title: A quantitative medium-throughput assay to measure Caenorhabditis elegans development and reproduction
protocol: Isolate eggs as described in step 3 of the “Before you begin” section.
Let eggs hatch for at least 12 h in the absence of food at 20°C in the dark while shaking gently in horizontal position to synchronize (L1 arrest).
Prepare fresh S-Complete medium.
Dilute OP50 suspension with S-Complete to desired concentration to keep worms and offspring well-fed over the 96 h incubation time.
Add chemicals of interest and solvent controls to diluted OP50 suspensions.
Concentrate solutions 1.25 fold higher than the desired final concentration.
Fill the 36 edge wells of a 96 well plate with 150 μL water.
Fill the 60 inner wells of the 96 well plate with 30 μL S-Complete.
Manually pick one synchronized L1 larva and place it in each inner well.
Use a 2.5 μL pipette for precise placement of larvae.
Ensure darkfield illumination is used during the process.
Prepare up to six plates per hour for experienced staff.
Use low retention tips when working with worms to prevent sticking.
Using a multistep pipette, add 120 μL of the master mix per well and note the exposure starting time.
Incubate plates for 96 h in a covered box at 20°C in the dark without shaking.
Stain worms and offspring with rose bengal.
Add 15 μL of rose bengal staining solution (300 mg/L in ddH2O) to each inner well of the plates.
Shake the plates vigorously at 900 rpm for 10 seconds to disperse worms, offspring, and food bacteria.
Heat the plates in an oven to 80°C for 20 minutes.
Add 100 μL ddH2O to each inner well and let the worms settle for at least 5 minutes.
Gently aspirate 100 μL of each well without aspirating worms and offspring using a preferably electronic 100 μL multi-channel pipette.
Repeat step 5d up to four times until most of the stain and bacteria has been removed.
Record images of whole wells using the Opera Phenix High Content Screening System (PerkinElmer, MA USA).
Use a 5× air objective and a fluorescence filter with emission from 570–630 nm, excitation at 561 nm, illumination time of 100 ms at 100% intensity to generate 9 tiles per well without overlap.
Use the device software "Harmony" (Perkin Elmer) to export measurements including TIFF images and XML metadata.
Install v.9.2 of the MATLAB Runtime on a Windows-based operating system.
Find the CombineTIFF.exe tool and associated CombineTIFF.m code in Mendeley Data.
Start “CombineTIFF.exe” and choose the Harmony export directory containing raw images and XML file.
Optionally give merged images a suffix, select channels to merge, and choose to merge images without overlap.
If single tiles are missing in a well, choose to skip those wells.
In the input folder, CombineTIFF generates a new folder named “combinedTIFFs” where merged images and an info TXT file are stored.
Import the merged images into the CellProfiler pipeline.
Use the filter option in the “Image” module if needed to filter out other channel images.
Select an output file location for the excel output files in the “ExportToSpreadsheet” module.
Choose the output file location of the output images in the six “SaveImages” modules.
Press the "Analyze Images" button.
Run one pipeline for each 96 well plate (60 images).
Define "Treatment 1" as wells B2–G6 and "Treatment 2" as wells B7–G11.
Open the CellProfiler output folder chosen in step 9b.
Locate the CSV output files “Test_data_Worms_4d.csv” and “Test_data_Worms_4d_small.csv” with suffix treatment identifier “_1” or “_2”.
Open the "Offspring.csv" file for information on identified objects for both treatments.
Convert the text in CellProfiler CSV output files into columns by separating with a comma.
Ensure Excel uses a point as decimal delimiter to avoid number alterations.
Create a new column named “Scoring” in each CSV file.
Check if the 4-day-old worms are correctly identified in the CellProfiler output images.
Score objects that were correctly identified as "0" in the "Scoring" column of the respective CSV file.
Score objects incorrectly identified or not meeting criteria as "1".
Register one score for each object in the “Scoring” column.
Save the modified files as CSV files.
Score objects as "1" if they are a) no actual 4-day-old worms, b) fragmented or cut 4-day-old worms, and c) major offspring appendages or multiple worms merged together.
Score 4-day-old worms with minor offspring appendages as "0".
